The design language that makes your AI harness better at design.

items.title: Show HN: Build with Python – a beginner course where your code draws
items.contentSnippet:
Hi HN, I built this because I watched my daughter struggle at learning Python. I made something that runs only in the browser with visuals rather than relying on CLI/terminal output. No need to worry about python installation, package versions, venv etc.
The lab runs with Pyodide in a web worker, and the program output is a picture by the side of the code block. A user would experiment with the code, and see the immediate changes in the visual output.

items.title: Show HN: Shlexball, describe a file and a local 1.5B model finds it on your Mac
items.contentSnippet:
Describe a file in plain English and Shlexball finds it on your Mac. Files stay local.
Base model: Qwen2.5 Coder 1.5B Instruct, fine tuned (SFT) by me to write search plans that a read only sandbox runs, on Apple's MLX.
FindBench (https://shlexball.com/findbench/), my benchmark, passes a test only on an exact file match. 312 tests unseen in training; other models got 30 examples:
  Model                  Params        Raw           With plural step (pilot)
  Shlexball              1.5B

items.title: Show HN: Exro – I got tired of cleaning up copy/paste between apps
items.contentSnippet:
Between Slack, Claude, GPT, and Gmail, I'm constantly making formatting changes: deleting timestamps and Slack's (edited), making API fields inline code, removing weird highlighting, etc.
I tried changing this with prompts, but for things like formatting rules, it didn't get applied consistently.
So I built Exro. It scans the pasted text and applies deterministic changes with no grammar/copy changes whatsoever. You can paste something in and try it directly. Let me know if you have any suggestio

items.title: Show HN: Jev-pages – Building landing pages real time with Jev
items.contentSnippet:
An experiment using Jev to generate landing pages in real time. Jev is great at picking between different options so I attempted to break down the langing page UI into a set of choices for the model to choose from.
How this works:
1. Users type what kind of page they want and Jev decides what each line is (headline, fact, assertion etc.)
